claim: The official Tailscale CLI docs mark 'tailscale status --json' output with an explicit warning that the format is subject to change, while simultaneously recommending it for automation tasks.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must treat the tailscale status JSON schema as unstable-by-policy: parse leniently, pin versions, and never assume field permanence
quoted_support: --json Output in JSON format (WARNING: format subject to change).

claim: 'tailscale wait' is the official readiness gate for services that bind to the Tailscale interface: it exits 0 when the interface and its IPs are available, and systemd users can depend on the tailscale-online.target unit which runs this command.
stance_target: on NixOS/jupiterOS, an MQTT-publishing agent should be ordered after tailscale-online.target (or invoke tailscale wait) instead of racing Tailscale at boot
scope_conditions: Tailscale v1.96+; as of v1.96 the only waitable resource is the Tailscale interface/IPs; userspace mode waits only for tailscaled + Running state
quoted_support:
Linux systemd users can wait for the tailscale-online.target target, which runs this command.

A service that wants to bind to (listen on) a Tailscale interface or IP address, can use the following pattern to ensure Tailscale is ready before the program starts:

tailscale wait && /path/to/service [...]

claim: The Tailscale CLI honours a global --socket=<path> flag to reach a tailscaled socket at a non-default location — essential on NixOS where socket paths may be customised per-host.
stance_target: the agent's tailscale collector must make the socket path configurable rather than assuming the default /var/run/tailscaled.socket
scope_conditions: common flag for all commands, Tailscale CLI
quoted_support:
Common flags for all commands:

--socket=<path> Path to the tailscaled socket.

claim: 'tailscale set --operator=<user>' designates a non-root Unix username allowed to operate tailscaled, providing the sanctioned mechanism for an unprivileged agent process to query and control the tailnet without root.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should run as a non-root service user and be granted tailscale access via --operator rather than running as root
quoted_support: --operator=<user>   Unix username other than root to operate tailscaled.

claim: 'tailscale ip --assert=<specific-ip-address>' provides an atomic assertion that a node has the expected Tailscale IP, composable with 'tailscale wait' for boot-time identity verification.
stance_target: fleet agents can verify per-host identity (expected 100.x IP) at startup before publishing telemetry tagged with that identity
quoted_support: --assert=<specific-ip-address> Assert that the node's IP (or one of the node's IPs) matches this IP address.

claim: 'tailscale netcheck --format=json' exposes machine-readable network-condition reports (UDP availability, IPv4/IPv6, NAT mapping variance, DERP latencies) usable as an agent-side network-quality sensor.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can publish WAN-side connectivity diagnostics (DERP relay fallback, NAT hardness) as MQTT sensors
quoted_support: --format=<format> Output format; empty (for human-readable), json or json-line.

claim: 'tailscale version' supports --json, --daemon (daemon vs client version), and --upstream (latest available release), giving an agent a three-way version comparison for client-drift detection.
stance_target: fleet-wide tailscale version drift can be sensed with one CLI invocation per host and no external API
quoted_support:
--daemon Also print local node's daemon version. Defaults to false.

--json Return a machine-readable JSON response.

--upstream Print the latest upstream release version from pkgs.tailscale.com.

claim: 'tailscale update --version=<explicit-version>' allows pinning the client to an exact version, and 'tailscale metrics print' exposes client metrics natively — both relevant to NixOS-style declarative version management and metrics exposure.
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet version management for the tailscale client
scope_conditions: tailscale update available v1.36+ on Windows and Ubuntu/Debian Linux (other distros may lack self-update, e.g. NixOS manages the package)
quoted_support: --version An explicit version to use for the update or downgrade.

claim: 'tailscale exit-node list' now supports filtering (--filter=<country>) alongside 'tailscale exit-node suggest', closing the gap that motivated feature request #9378.
stance_target: exit-node selection state is now CLI-addressable with structured options rather than regex-parsing column output
quoted_support:
Available flags for list:

--filter=<country> Filter exit nodes by country.

claim: Tailscale offers 'tailscale configure systray --enable-startup=systemd' for Linux desktop systray integration (v1.88+), illustrating that Tailscale itself ships systemd-unit installation flows the agent ecosystem can mirror.
stance_target: patterns for shipping systemd-enabled Linux client components
quoted_support: --enable-startup=<init-system> Install the startup script for the init system. The only currently supported value is systemd.
